features: Settings now has two buttons that check the AI really works instead of just reporting that it is installed. "Test on sample pages" runs handwriting recognition on two real scanned work samples and tells you how much of the handwriting it read. "Test AI models" asks each model role a question with a known answer and reports each role as working, responding with a wrong answer, or not working.
bugs: Fixed another case of the Finalize button going missing. Work Sample Buddy was checking a student's work against every school year at once instead of just the current one, so an unfinished course left over from last year could block packaging forever — the student showed "0 samples due" with no way to finalize them.
Fixed being unable to remove a student, delete a course, or rebuild a learning period after using "Require its own sample" on one of their courses. The action failed and left everything unchanged.

When a step needed an AI model that is not installed, the message named a model you never chose and offered no way forward. It now offers to switch to models already on your computer, or to open Settings.
Fixed the "model not installed" warning still appearing while analysing a document, naming a model that was never chosen.
Fixed Work Sample Buddy reporting "qwen3.5:4b not installed" when no grading model had been chosen. With no model set it now uses one you actually have installed.
Restore Defaults no longer leaves a model role pointing at a model that is not installed.
Fixed being unable to remove a student, delete a course, or rebuild a learning period after using "Require its own sample" on one of their courses. The action failed and left everything unchanged.

Fixed another case of the Finalize button going missing. Work Sample Buddy was checking a student's work against every school year at once instead of just the current one, so an unfinished course left over from last year could block packaging forever — the student showed "0 samples due" with no way to finalize them.
Fixed the "model not installed" warning still appearing while analysing a document, naming a model that was never chosen.

features: Settings now has two buttons that check the AI really works instead of just reporting that it is installed. "Test on sample pages" runs handwriting recognition on two real scanned work samples and tells you how much of the handwriting it read. "Test AI models" asks each model role a question with a known answer and reports each role as working, responding with a wrong answer, or not working.
bugs: When a step needed an AI model that is not installed, the message named a model you never chose and offered no way forward. It now offers to switch to models already on your computer, or to open Settings.
Fixed Work Sample Buddy reporting "qwen3.5:4b not installed" when no grading model had been chosen. With no model set it now uses one you actually have installed.
Restore Defaults no longer leaves a model role pointing at a model that is not installed.

features: You can now require a work sample from one specific TK-8 core course. Right-click a course showing "Satisfied" and choose "Require its own sample" — it goes back to needing its own sample while the other core courses stay as they are. Right-click it again to undo. Previously right-clicking a satisfied course did nothing at all.
On Mac, text recognition now uses Apple's built-in Vision engine, which is faster, needs no download and cannot be broken by a missing component.
bugs: Fixed the Finalize button disappearing at the start of a new school year. Students who had finished everything showed "0 samples due" with no way to package them, and Finalize All found nobody. Work Sample Buddy was measuring this year's courses against last year's learning period dates.
Fixed packages being built from the wrong school year's date range, which could produce an empty package or a file named with last year's month.
Fixed a crash that could close the app without warning while you were working. The automatic update check ran in the background and could collide with whatever you were doing.
Fixed text recognition being completely unavailable on Mac. Two required components were left out of the Mac build, and Mac had no other engine to fall back on.

features: Students and courses you add yourself are now kept separate from the ones Pathways sends, and a sync no longer removes them. They appear in the completion matrix with their requirements already created, and importing or exporting a course list remembers which records are yours.

TK-8 core subjects can now require either one combined work sample or a separate sample for each core course. Set it for the whole school under Settings > Grading & Output, per learning period and optionally for a single school year, or right-click one student in the matrix to set it just for them.

Source folders can now be marked Annual or Permanent. Annual folders switch off when the school year changes, and you can add one stable parent folder holding year folders such as 25-26 SY so only the current year is scanned.
First-run setup now walks you through connecting the PCA Chrome extension, tells you what to do if Chrome or the extension is missing, and offers to bring in your student roster.
bugs: The roster import preview is accurate again: it no longer warns that students will be removed when they will be kept, shows student ID numbers when two students share a name, lets you protect a student without leaving the preview, and adds course totals up correctly. This also covers imports made through the Pathways browser extension.
Prior-year folders under a stable source parent are no longer picked up by automatic imports.
Drawing or erasing on a large page in the PDF ink editor no longer slows the app down or uses up memory, and the blue selection box is now labelled so it is clear where you can draw.
Update checks no longer fail silently. If they have been failing for several days, Settings > Status now tells you.
The folder row and its duration menu are no longer clipped in Settings, and the table now follows both light and dark themes.
A missing workspace at startup now offers a Quit option instead of forcing you to continue.
Fixed Settings incorrectly reporting the PCA Chrome extension as missing when it was installed in developer mode.

features: Added first-run guidance to help teachers connect the PCA Chrome extension and confirm that it is working.
Added a visible onboarding step that asks teachers about importing their student roster.
bugs: Fixed missing-workspace prompts so teachers can choose Quit instead of being forced to continue startup.

The import preview now shows student ID numbers when two students share a name, and lets you protect a student from removal without leaving the preview. Course totals add up correctly, and inactive historical records no longer trigger repeated warnings.
Update checks are more reliable and no longer fail silently. If checks have been failing for several days, Settings → Status will now tell you.

Drawing or erasing on a large page in the PDF ink editor no longer slows the app down or eats memory. The editor now sizes its working image to the selection instead of rendering the whole page at full resolution.
The ink editor labels the blue selection box, so it is clear where you can draw.
The import preview no longer warns that a manually added student will be removed. Students marked "keep through Pathways syncs" are now shown as kept, and the roster count no longer drops by one.
Fixed the warning still appearing when importing through the Pathways browser extension, which was the most common way to hit it.

features: Source folders now show an Annual or Permanent setting directly beside each path. Annual folders deactivate when the school year changes, while Permanent folders stay active.
You can now add one stable parent folder containing year folders such as 25-26 SY and 26-27 SY. Work Sample Buddy automatically scans only the current school year's folder.
bugs: Prior-year folders under a stable source parent are no longer included in automatic imports.
The folder row and its duration menu are no longer clipped in Settings, and the table now follows both light and dark themes.
Fixed the roster import preview so it no longer warns that students will be removed when they will actually be kept, and now clearly shows the setting responsible.

features: Students and courses you add yourself are now kept separate from the ones Pathways sends, and a sync no longer removes them. If you add a course to a student who came from Pathways, that student is treated as yours from then on.
Students you add in Setup now show up in the completion matrix with their work sample requirements already created for every learning period.

TK-8 core subjects can now require either one combined work sample or a separate sample for each core course. Set it for the whole school under Settings > Grading & Output, per learning period, and optionally for just one school year.

You can also set the core sample count for a single student by right-clicking them in the matrix. It applies from that learning period onward, including into later school years, until you set a different one. Clearing it goes back to whatever was in effect before. The option is hidden for high school students.
Importing and exporting a course list now records whether each student and course is yours or came from Pathways, so importing one course no longer takes over the whole student.
bugs: Students and courses added by hand no longer disappear the next time Pathways syncs.

features: Grades now use ADV, PRO, DEV and MIN alongside the usual letter grades, replacing the old check-mark symbols. These marks carry no point value of their own inside Work Sample Buddy, and post to Schoology as the matching letter grade so your gradebook still totals correctly.

From the 2026-2027 school year, learning periods 3, 5 and 7 need a separate work sample for each TK-8 core subject: Language Arts, Mathematics, Science and Social Studies. Earlier school years, other learning periods, elective courses and high school are unchanged.
About & help is now available in Simple Mode instead of being hidden behind the advanced settings.
bugs: Dropping a Word document no longer freezes the app for around two minutes the first time you do it. Conversions now finish in a couple of seconds.
The completion matrix no longer goes blank when the school year rolls over.
Replacing a file in Simple Mode no longer discards the file you dropped.

Work Sample Buddy no longer asks again about an update you have already answered, and two update checks can no longer race each other into downloading the same installer twice. Older downloaded installers are tidied up, keeping only the two most recent.
The grading window now reports an unsupported grade mark instead of quietly doing nothing.

The uninstaller now always tells you that your settings and student roster are shared by both the Beta and the regular version, and that there is only one copy. It also keeps them, and explains why, when it cannot confirm which Windows account installed the app.

The uninstaller now always tells you that your settings and student roster are shared by both the Beta and the regular version, and that there is only one copy. Before, that warning only appeared when the other version happened to still be installed, which is exactly when those options were switched off anyway.

The uninstaller no longer risks removing the wrong Windows account's settings. If it is run by a different user than the one who installed the app, for example when an administrator types their password to allow it, it now keeps your settings and roster and explains why instead of deleting files it cannot identify.

features: When you uninstall Work Sample Buddy, it now asks what you want to remove. The program is uninstalled as always, and you separately choose whether to also delete your settings, the student roster and grading database, downloaded update files, or logs. Everything is unchecked to begin with, so nothing extra is removed unless you ask for it.
The uninstaller never deletes your work samples or your workspace folder, whichever boxes you tick.
bugs: Fixed the Check for Updates button being pushed off the right edge of the Status and health page when a release had long update notes.

The Notify me of new updates setting now actually stops update prompts. Before this, the setting only applied inside Settings, so the app still asked about updates shortly after launch and again every hour.
Fixed every document being fully re-analysed each time when the AI model was unavailable, which made things slower on computers not running Ollama.
Recent Updates now reads release notes written for Windows, so they are no longer replaced by notes from a Mac release.
If you have both the Beta and the regular version installed, uninstalling one no longer offers to delete the shared student roster and settings that the other one still needs.

features: Work Sample Buddy now keeps only the two most recent downloaded updates instead of every one it has ever fetched, freeing up disk space.
bugs: Fixed two Update windows opening at once and downloading the same file twice, which could end in an error and leave the update unfinished.
Checking for updates no longer re-downloads an update you have already downloaded.
If you choose 'Not now', Work Sample Buddy stops asking about that version until you check again yourself.
An update you chose to install later is no longer offered again as a fresh download.

features: If the app ever fails to open on a Mac, it now tells you why. You get a window with the error, ready to copy, and the address to send it to - no Terminal, no hunting for log files.

In LP3, LP5 and LP7, TK-8 students now need one work sample for each core subject - Math, English, History and Science. A single sample no longer covers the other three. Other learning periods, high school, and previous school years are unchanged.
Grading now uses ADV, PRO, DEV and MIN instead of symbol marks.
Those marks now post to Schoology and stay put when you sync again.
bugs: Fixed first-run setup getting stuck on 'Waiting for the PCA Extension'. If you installed the extension before Work Sample Buddy, the two could never connect. Setup now connects on its own, and never leaves you stuck waiting.
Fixed setup suggesting the previous teacher's name on a shared computer.
Fixed dropping a Word document freezing the app for up to two minutes.
Word documents you have already converted now reopen much faster.
Fixed Simple mode throwing away the file you dropped onto Replace.
Fixed the Mac app failing to open on computers that don't have developer tools installed. It closed instantly with no error message and no log file.
Fixed the Mac app failing to launch on some machines because of a conflicting system library.

features: About and help information is now available in Simple Mode; developer tools stay in Advanced.
bugs: The completion matrix no longer goes blank when the school year rolls over.
The Chrome extension bridge on Mac is now a signed, self-contained component and no longer fails to start.
Printing web pages to PDF no longer hangs, and the page footer no longer shows a local file path.
Beta builds no longer offer an already-installed update as if it were new.
Re-start, Redo, and Restart now ask for confirmation before discarding a sample that is waiting for verification and re-running extraction, so verify-stage work can't be lost by a stray click.

features: Large PDFs, student packages, and page thumbnails now load and process in the background, so the window stays responsive during heavy work.
Lower memory use when viewing large documents and long page strips.
bugs: Fixed rare crashes and file corruption when saving, rotating, or replacing PDFs during grading and review.
Google Drive and Schoology 'Test Connection' and folder scans no longer freeze the app while they run.
More reliable cancellation of long-running compression and folder-scan operations.
Faster, more responsive startup.
Maintenance release: build and release tooling fixes. No changes to the app itself.

features: New OCR engine: switched to PaddleOCR PP-OCRv6 (tiny) as the primary handwriting reader with a WinOCR fallback — smaller install and better accuracy on student work.
OCR effort modes now scale how many pages are scanned: Quick reads 1 page, Balanced 4 (with smart last-page coverage), and Thorough reads every page.
New "Off — OCR only" mode runs text extraction without Ollama/AI grading, for when you just want the text.
bugs: Fixed OCR not working in the installed (frozen) build — PaddleX initialization, bundled dependencies, and package metadata.
Fixed graded feedback not repopulating when you regrade a sample.
Fixed an intermittent crash when the student matrix refreshed during its fade-in animation.
Fixed the AI settings falsely labelling a model "not vision-capable" when it simply was not installed on the selected Ollama host — it now says it could not verify.

features: Added automatic update notifications to help you stay current with the latest features.
Improved the update process by moving to a more reliable download system on GitHub.

bugs: Fixed an issue where the app could show a previous update as if it were a new one after already installing it
Fixed a crash that could occur when choosing "Install Later" on the update prompt
Fixed an issue where the app sometimes didn't reopen automatically after installing an update

features: The app now asks before downloading an update, so it only happens when you're ready — and you can keep working while it downloads in the background

bugs: Fixed an issue on Mac where the update installer couldn't find the app to replace after downloading
Fixed the update checker so it correctly identifies the latest update for your platform (Mac or Windows) and doesn't mix them up

features: Work Sample Buddy can now update itself — when a new version is available, you'll see a prompt to install it right from the app, with no need to manually download and reinstall. Works on both Mac and Windows.
Added a first-run Welcome Wizard that guides new teachers through initial setup, plus new interactive Quick Start tutorials that demonstrate how to scan, organize, and package student work samples

Redesigned the Settings menu with a cleaner, accordion-style layout: each configuration section now expands one at a time to reduce clutter, and all panels (Grading Rules, PDF Output, Schoology, and more) have been compacted to fit more options on screen with less scrolling
Improved the Progress Grid with smoother data refreshing and clearer visual overlays when checking which students have submitted work samples
bugs: Fixed a crash that occurred when clicking Cancel in the Settings window
Fixed error handling to gracefully notify you if required AI models are missing when using Simple Mode, instead of failing silently

features: Improved AI grading with hardware auto-tuning, throttled background processing to prevent computer slowdown, one-click fixes for missing AI models, and better recognition of handwritten headers

Added accelerated math standards support to report card comments with new "Clear Period" controls, and enhanced the progress grid with polished Schoology badges, faster imports, and smarter finalization gating
Sped up PDF previews and the grading viewer with background thumbnail generation, adjacent page prefetching, and cached orientation detection
Added PCA Chrome extension diagnostics with path mismatch detection and improved onboarding rechecks
bugs: Fixed crashes when deleting courses with unfinished report card drafts or when dragging to reorder pages in previews, plus corrected pending sample badge counts, OCR setup issues, and report card general comment generation failures

features: Pathways uploads now detect when Chrome opened the upload page and keep waiting through sign-in prompts instead of failing early.
bugs: Pathways uploads now fail faster with clearer Chrome profile guidance when the PCA Extension never sees the upload tab.
Installed Windows and Mac builds now include the native bridge upload acknowledgement helper needed by the PCA Extension.
Windows builds now bundle the native bridge upload-date helper inside wsb_bridge.exe, preventing repeated Pathways bridge startup popups
Mac builds now include the native bridge upload-date helper, preventing Pathways upload bridge startup failures after installing on macOS

features: Pathways uploads now show queued upload state, support queued re-upload confirmation, and keep the upload controls clearer while another student is uploading
Matrix review flags now have a fuller review workflow for flagged students and samples
Package finalization now gives clearer missing-file handling when a sample PDF has moved or disappeared
bugs: Pathways uploads now match students against the requested school-year roster and block uploads when completed-work dates do not fit the requested LP/year slot
Upload failures that happen before file injection now report the real preflight error back to Work Sample Buddy instead of timing out without a debug log
Student upload flags are cleared after upload, and course work-sample flags are cleared after a finalized packet is created
AI and grading queue background work now uses tighter runtime limits and responsiveness checks to reduce long-running stalls

features: AI model settings now use clearer Light, Medium, and Heavy roles, with optional task-specific models and a Use for All shortcut for teachers who want one model everywhere
The Schoology grading course selector now includes clearer course progress details, including overall grade and missing-work counts
Setup integrations are split into clearer File Imports, Schoology, and Google Drive sections that load directly in the setup view
bugs: AI feedback cleanup now removes forced or uncertain critical comments instead of posting unsupported correction advice
PDF grading and patch tools now use smaller focused helpers for page edits, patch rendering, text patches, and marker overlays, reducing reload and traceback failures
Several Qt UI paths now guard deleted widgets and pixmap compatibility edge cases that could cause intermittent crashes

features: Finalized matrix rows now use a polished Schoology badge that opens the selected student's Schoology coursework, with a notification dot when new unposted work is waiting
bugs: Schoology video submissions now run the foreground Whisper transcript the first time they are opened after pre-grade, even when pre-grade already created a PDF preview
Switching courses in the Schoology grading window now stays scoped to the selected student instead of opening the first student in the class
Finalized student rows now keep showing unposted Schoology work even while it is still waiting for pre-grade

features: Teachers can now update a Schoology task from the grading window and queue a re-grade that uses the revised task, with clearer queue messages while it runs
Course right-click menus now include Schoology pre-grading controls when a course has queued or analyzing submissions
bugs: Schoology refresh now commits local roster and assignment updates before checking submissions or resubmission threads, avoiding open-transaction errors during API calls
Merging into an existing pending sample now resolves workspace-relative source files and warns when the original files are missing
PDF link copying now preserves supported external link types while skipping internal page-jump links whose page numbers can change
Learning-period calendar notification menus now clean up stale popups without closing a newer menu
Rejected-date feedback now distinguishes weekend dates from holiday and non-school-day dates

features: Patch Selected Area now includes a dedicated ink correction workflow with grab-pen sampling, adjustable pen, halo, paper, eraser, softness, and blotchiness controls
Ink corrections now preview and render sampled handwriting details more naturally, including color variation, halo behavior, circular eraser sizing, and live eraser outlines
Typed text replacement now shows the detected font details and auto-aligns replacement text unless the user manually changes the alignment
bugs: PDF patching now keeps edits attached to the correct editable Schoology source document instead of losing changes after reload, undo, or header/task rebuilds
Ink and eraser patches now avoid gray border artifacts around edited strokes and patch rectangles
Patch dialogs now open away from the selected PDF area and shut down pending preview work when closed, avoiding crashes after closing the dialog
Version bumping now rolls 4.1.99 to 4.2.00 instead of 4.1.100
Family contact messages now honor saved course checkbox selections immediately when the contact window is reopened
Family contact Gmail actions no longer queue duplicate pending messages, and reminders for different learning periods stay separate
Schoology image submissions that open as converted PDFs now use the current revision correctly instead of treating the PDF as a stale copy of the original image
Gradebook printout feedback now uses the detected saved grade and course when the submitted page has little or no readable text
Packaged builds now keep required Google API support modules available, preventing frozen-app failures from missing standard library dependencies
Schoology grading now removes the first page from the actual editable submission source, rebuilds any active header/task/link stamps, and keeps the remaining pages renumbered correctly
K8 sibling status refreshes no longer crash after a background extraction fails and its worker has already been cleaned up
Opening a student's input folder from the matrix no longer raises an error on macOS
Preview auto-coordinate lookup now ignores malformed background results instead of crashing the preview window

features: Schoology grading now detects newer resubmission notices from the submission thread during refresh and grading-window load, so returned revisions are picked up even when Schoology keeps the same filename
Large phone-photo submissions are handled with safer OCR and preview scaling, improving extraction on oversized JPEGs without forcing slow full-resolution scans
bugs: Cached Schoology attachments are now validated against current Schoology file metadata before reuse, preventing an older LP/sample file from appearing after a same-name resubmission
HTML placeholder and Google-link submissions now resolve to the current PDF before header or task stamping, avoiding stale base files during grading
Video submissions no longer restart pre-grading while conversion is already running
Generated task descriptions now use larger response budgets and reject mid-sentence endings, so task text no longer stops after phrases like "including" or "detailing"
The packaged-sample banner no longer clips the message when the right-side status chip is hidden
Vision extraction now rejects obvious book or page numbers as grades and can correct OCR year slips when the corrected date fits the LP range

features: Large Schoology video uploads now create a smaller temporary MP4 before uploading to Google Drive, keeping the original local video untouched and falling back to the original if compression is unavailable or not worthwhile
bugs: Finalized rows whose combined PDF is missing now offer to rebuild the finalized package from the student's existing completed samples instead of stopping at a file-not-found popup
The Task checkbox now stamps explicit Schoology task instructions onto activity-log submissions when real instructions are present, while still avoiding generic activity-log boilerplate
Checking Task now applies the task stamp when the PDF does not already have one, even if analysis already detected task text

features: Advanced verification manual tagging now stays manual: placing, moving, or resizing a tag no longer runs region OCR automatically, and tag OCR is available from the right-click Scan Tag Text action when needed
bugs: Switching out of Demo DB no longer lets the internal demo workspace become the real workspace, preventing older sample paths from being expanded under demo_workspace
Workspace-relative sample paths can now recover through recent real workspaces when a stale workspace root points at the wrong folder
Config loading now tolerates UTF-8 BOM files, preventing a valid saved workspace from being ignored after external config edits
Family contact status messages no longer raise a deleted QLabel error if the dialog closes before a delayed status clear runs
Google Drive source refreshes now write sign-in and scan failures to the app log, so a failed Drive login is visible after the popup is gone
Transient Google Drive token hiccups now get one quiet retry before Buddy asks you to sign in again, reducing unnecessary popups when Drive recovers by itself
Matrix refresh now keeps Google Drive sign-in or scan problems visible in the refresh status instead of replacing them with a generic sync-complete message

features: Schoology video submissions can now be uploaded directly to Google Drive from the grading window, creating an anyone-with-link URL and stamping it onto the submission when +Link is enabled
Source folder imports now support fuzzy course matching with confirmation prompts, remembered acceptances, and better filename parsing for PCA/PPS and season-prefixed files
The Schoology grading panel now separates posting grades from packaging work samples: the LP sample banner packages, replaces, or removes the Buddy sample independently from Post/Repost
A synthetic demo database mode is available for walkthroughs and recordings without using real student data
bugs: Post to thread is no longer persistent: it starts off for every loaded Schoology submission and only posts to the thread when enabled for that specific submission
Removing a pending sample whose source file is missing no longer crashes after the missing-file recovery dialog
Schoology grading now blocks normal grades on missing submissions unless the grade is Mi or Ex, avoiding accidental real grades on missing work
Google Drive source scans now offer a sign-in recovery prompt when the saved Drive token cannot be refreshed

features: Schoology grading now reads as accept/reject: the green dropdown shows "Accepted" instead of "No flag", reasons mark the submission as "Rejected", and the matrix and notification surfaces label rejected Schoology submissions clearly while keeping the matrix "flagged" feature for completed samples separate

Family contact emails for missing samples now announce repeat sends as "2nd attempt", "3rd attempt", and so on in the email banner, intro, plain text, and brief, so families can tell this is a follow-up reminder

The report card comment dialog has a new "Copy for Magic School" button that builds the same structured prompt and copies it to the clipboard, so teachers can paste it into Magic School, ChatGPT, or Claude when Ollama is not running
The Thread back-arrow next to the submission thread label is now a clickable button that opens the thread, matching the bigger Thread button next to it
bugs: Resubmissions now download the actual new revision: cached attachments are validated against Schoology's md5 before reuse, so a student's resubmitted file is never silently replaced by the previous revision when filenames match

When a stale revision is detected, the submission's prior AI, final, and posted grade/comment fields are cleared so the form picks up the fresh AI analysis of the new file instead of reapplying the old grade
Opening a missing-file submission in the grading window now clears and collapses the page strip so thumbnails from the previous submission no longer appear above the "No file available" message
Family contact dialog and emails now distinguish Schoology-rejected submissions from matrix-flagged completed samples instead of merging both into one Flagged count

features: Schoology Google Docs and Google Drive link submissions can now be resolved into PDFs during grading when Google Drive export credentials are available, with a Schoology converted-PDF fallback when export is unavailable
The Schoology submission thread now supports quick inline teacher replies, editing teacher comments, and deleting teacher comments from the grading window
Duplicate submission warnings now list matching submissions directly in the grading panel so the original and duplicate files can be opened and compared
The work-sample packaging confirmation screen and course picker now make the student, Schoology course, and Pathways LP course clearer and filter choices to the student's relevant LP courses
AI performance presets now control background pre-grading more explicitly, so Quick mode stays lighter while Balanced and Thorough can do more work
bugs: Schoology submission delete is shown as unavailable when the teacher/API role cannot delete submission revisions, avoiding a failed action that Schoology returns as HTTP 403
The grading panel uses a denser task/feedback layout so Course Progress has more room, and AI-generated feedback is visually marked in the feedback label
Auto-grade completion summaries now count completed priority and batch items correctly instead of reporting zero when work actually finished
Matrix notification summaries now include clearer counts for Schoology flags, manual review items, unread comments, and calendar categories
Duplicate detection ignores stale hashes for submissions whose local file was cleared, reducing false duplicate flags after re-downloads or cleanup

features: TK-8 core-course samples can now be kept on file but removed from the current LP package from the course right-click menu, then added back later if that PDF should be the packaged sample
The Schoology grading workflow now asks before overwriting an existing Buddy sample, reducing accidental replacement when packaging a submission into an LP slot that already has work
Right-click menus throughout the app now include visual icons or emoji cues, making grading, preview tagging, matrix, PDF, queue, tray, page-strip, and setup actions easier to scan
bugs: Not-packaged TK-8 samples stay saved without being counted in final LP packages, duplicate staged imports, or shared-sample completion checks
After posting a Schoology grade, the grading window now switches cleanly from Post to Repost after the brief Posted confirmation
Header/task stamp status now appears in the main grading toolbar status area instead of taking extra space in the grading panel
Preview badge right-click menus in simple mode now open at the clicked position instead of offset from the badge

features: The Schoology grading window has a cleaner, denser right panel with compact date, flag, stamp, task, feedback, score, course, and progress controls that leave more room for reading feedback
Feedback processing depth is now visible from the grading toolbar, with diagnostics and processing settings grouped into the same menu
Course Progress now includes a segmented progress meter for graded, flagged, and open work, and stronger work-sample candidates are emphasized directly in the list

Right-clicking the Post/Repost button or LP sample checkbox now shows focused sample-only actions, including using the current work as the LP sample without reposting feedback, replacing the existing LP sample, or removing the current sample
bugs: When a previously flagged Schoology submission is resubmitted, stale F/0 flag grades and generic feedback no longer block the fresh pre-grade result from filling the form
Blank generated task text now remains inspectable in the grading workflow, and generic assignment titles such as LP Samples are no longer reused as assignment task text
One-page submissions now collapse the thumbnail strip automatically while keeping a View pages control available
Page selection mode now builds all selectable thumbnails immediately, so select all, deselect, rotate selected, and group controls work reliably

features: Schoology grading now has a dedicated Wrong date flag for work samples dated outside the current learning period. The feedback tells the student the incorrect sample date and the expected LP date range
The Schoology grading window now warns before you leave or close a flagged submission that has not been posted yet, so an F/0 resubmission flag is not accidentally left local-only

Grading prompts are more cautious about handwriting, readability, and inferred task requirements, reducing feedback that criticizes neatness or claims a missing requirement that was not explicitly provided
bugs: Next in the Schoology grading window now skips flagged submissions that were already posted and advances to the next unposted item, while still stopping on flagged submissions that have not been posted yet
Unchecking + Task now hides the task editor consistently, even after AI/header analysis finds task text
Image-heavy grading submissions can skip slow full-page OCR when vision field scan is available, and Ollama grading requests now cap context and response size to avoid runaway slowdowns
Preview coordinate matching is more reliable for split/cropped pages and generated preview PDFs, including source-coordinate fallback when preview search would hit an old stamped header
Windows OCR and image-orientation checks now close PIL image handles promptly, reducing file-handle leaks during long grading and preview sessions

Mac builds now explicitly bundle all Work Sample Buddy source modules, including the new visible-score grading helper. This fixes Heat AI failing in the packaged app with "No module named 'src.core.visible_score'" even when git pull said the source was up to date

Closing the app while the grading queue is active no longer lets a late worker-finished signal start another pending batch during shutdown, preventing the "QThread: Destroyed while thread is still running" crash

features: Grading now treats a visible teacher or platform score on the submission as the source of truth. Scores found in the text, OCR boxes, top margin, or vision field scan are carried into Grade/Points, and full-credit visible scores no longer produce feedback that claims mistakes or missing work

Activity logs and skills sheets now use assignment profiles based on the Schoology title/description. Plain "Log" and "Skills" assignments skip separate task detection, use the correct grading guidance, and override stale work-sample assignment types when needed

Grading effort presets now have clearer behavior: Fast stays text-only, Balanced uses a small capped vision pass, and Thorough can inspect more images while keeping text prompts within an effort-specific budget

Family contact now shows clearer previous-contact history, updates the matrix after a send or draft succeeds, and handles middle-school core course selections more precisely when a user selects individual courses
The grading queue now keeps canceled, paused, queued, and actively analyzing submissions in sync across the matrix, queue dialog, and grading window
bugs: Image-heavy submissions with only partial OCR text no longer get graded from Schoology page controls. If a visible LMS score is present, Work Sample Buddy uses that score without inventing feedback; otherwise it leaves the item for vision grading or manual review

PDF header/task/link stamping now preserves pages that already have PDF rotation metadata, and the analyzer resets misapplied rotation metadata before OCR or vision checks so rotated phone-photo PDFs do not get read sideways
Closing a grading window now detaches from the shared grading queue instead of canceling work that is still running elsewhere
Manual task overrides are cleared more cleanly on reset/resubmission, including the mirrored detected-task field when it was only storing the old override

"Task is Wrong" → Save & Re-grade now actually uses the corrected task. The override was being saved correctly to the submission and shown in the form, but the grading worker was still building its prompt from Schoology's original assignment description, so the re-grade produced identical feedback. The worker now reads user_task_override first and feeds it into the grading prompt as the assignment description

features: "Fix Task" renamed to "Clean Task" and a new "Task is Wrong" button sits next to it. Click "Task is Wrong" to open an editor with the current task description; rewrite what the assignment really asks for and click Save & Re-grade. Your text is persisted on the submission as the source of truth, the analyzer uses it instead of generating its own task description, and a fresh analysis is queued immediately. The override sticks until the student resubmits (the resubmission flow clears it because the prior correction may not apply to the new revision)

bugs: Re-grade confirmation dialog no longer mentions "AI" — the message is now "Re-grading will replace [it/them] with a fresh analysis" and the title is just "Re-grade?"

features: AI feedback now gets a humanizing pass before it lands on the form or in the database. The grading prompt already tells the model to address the student directly, but it slips into third-person "the student" anyway. The post-process replaces "the student" / "this student" (and possessive forms with both straight and curly apostrophes) with the student's first name, so feedback reads "Asher adapted the assignment" rather than "the student adapted the assignment." Sentence-start capitalization is preserved when a substitution lands after a period

bugs: Audio-only submission PDFs no longer waste page 1 on a header alone — the transcript now flows immediately under the file name + duration on the same page and continues onto page 2 only when the content actually overflows. A short audio submission that previously rendered as 3 pages will fit on 2

features: Audio-only submissions (.mp3 / .m4a / .wav / .aac / .ogg / .flac / .wma / .opus) now skip the video-frame extraction path and go straight to transcription. The MP4 ftyp magic bytes are shared by MP4 video AND audio-only formats like .m4a, so the file-kind sniffer was routing audio files through cv2.VideoCapture which hangs on Windows trying to demux a video track that doesn't exist. Now the converter detects the audio extension and produces a transcript-on-its-own-page PDF without ever calling cv2 — fixes the 90-second wedge the user reported on an .m4a submission
bugs: First-time submission download now stamps the cached file's revision id into ai_header_check so the next _check_stale_cache pass doesn't trip the stale-cache cascade (which would clear the AI/final fields then re-download the same file in a loop). v4.1.70 fixed this for Re-download specifically; this extends the fix to any download that creates a fresh cache entry

Course Progress list now shows the 📦 packaged badge (and the WS banner shows "packaged") when the date resolver found the published sample via requirement_id but methods 1-3 missed it. The packaged-sub detection chain that feeds the 📦 emoji now includes the same fourth fallback as the date resolver — work_samples joined by the WS-banner-resolved requirement id — so the date and the badge agree on whether this sub is the published one

Auto-apply on PDF load now uses the same field-availability check as the manual checkbox toggle (name/date/course resolvable) instead of the stricter has_name/has_date/has_course flags that only AI extraction sets. After Re-download, the header_check is reset to a revision stub with none of those flags, so the auto-apply was silently skipping the header even when the checkbox was on — toggling off-and-on then worked because the manual handler uses the permissive check. Now both paths agree

Added a fourth fallback for the date resolver: read work_samples.work_date by the requirement id resolved via the WS-banner. Catches published samples whose schoology_submission_id is NULL AND whose file path doesn't carry sub_{id}_ (e.g. samples imported via the matrix Inputs flow with renamed filenames). The resolver now also logs the source label (direct / legacy_path / pending_samples / requirement_id / none) so the chosen date's origin is visible
Added _load_pdf logging: every reload prints `_load_pdf: sub=N file=basename load_ok=True/False` so the empty-viewer-after-fix issue can be traced from the log

features: Header and Task stamps now apply automatically when their checkboxes are on after the PDF loads. Previously you had to uncheck-and-recheck the box to trigger the stamp because form populate sets the checkbox state with signals blocked. Now _load_pdf calls the existing _auto_apply_missing_fixes hook once the PDF is visible — the stamp matches the checkbox state without manual toggling

Packaged work samples now save the as-posted task description and feedback text alongside the file. Stored on both pending_samples and work_samples (new task_text and feedback_text columns), and also embedded in the metadata JSON. Lets future tooling re-post to Schoology, audit, or display the original post without re-running AI
bugs: Fixed AttributeError that crashed the grading window after Re-download — _load_pdf was calling a method I'd named differently than the existing helper

Date resolver now also checks pending_samples — a submission packaged via "Use as LP sample" lives there with metadata.date BEFORE the import flow promotes it into work_samples. The WS-banner detection already checks all three locations (work_samples direct + work_samples legacy path + pending_samples); the date resolver was missing the pending_samples branch, so freshly packaged subs would keep falling back to submitted_at instead of restoring the date the user entered when packaging

Date resolver now finds work samples whose schoology_submission_id column was never populated (legacy data published before that column was being saved). Falls back to matching `sub_{id}_…` in the source / output PDF path — same legacy fallback the unpackage flow uses. Also exposes the match source (direct vs legacy_path) in the diagnostic log line

Added diagnostic logs for the completion-date resolver so the picked date is provable from the log: every form populate now writes `_populate_form date pick: sub=X → PICKED (final=A ai=B posted_cmt=C thread_cmt=D ext=E)` showing every source and the winner, plus a `Date resolver:` line listing both work_samples.work_date and submitted_at with the priority decision and reason

features: Date field on the grading form now restores from a published work sample first — if you've already published this submission as a sample to the student's matrix, that's the canonical date and it comes back when you re-open or Re-download. For non-published or never-published submissions it falls back to the Schoology submitted_at timestamp. Resubmissions skip the published-sample date (it belongs to the old revision) and use submitted_at directly

bugs: Fixed numeric grades crashing the Schoology metadata parser. Schoology's grades response returns `grade` as a float (9.5) for numeric assignments and a string for letter grades; the parser was calling .strip() on the value unconditionally, which threw AttributeError on every numeric grade and bailed out before storing posted_grade or posted_comment. Both reconcile and Re-download now coerce values to string before stripping

Re-download no longer trips a stale-cache cascade that wiped the AI/final fields a second time. The flow was: Re-download cleared ai_header_check (correct, since fix flags belong to the old file) → _load_pdf called _check_stale_cache → stored_rev was None and current_rev was the new revision, so the cache was always "stale" → clears AI/final and re-downloads in a loop. The clear now stamps ai_header_check with the current revision id, so the stale check sees a match and leaves the just-restored data alone

Re-download now actually finds the grade and feedback in Schoology's response. The old parser only walked period[].grade[] and section[].period[].grade[], but Schoology's grades endpoint also returns rows at the top level (under `grades`) and with the inner key spelled `grades` instead of `grade`, depending on the section. A response with rows in any of those positions was being read as 0 grade rows — so Re-download silently treated graded subs as ungraded and ran AI. The new walker recursively yields every grade entry it can find regardless of where it sits in the response shape, and reconcile uses the same walker

Re-download no longer silently runs AI and fills fabricated defaults ("A" 100/100, submitted_at as the date) when the Schoology grade fetch fails or doesn't match. The handler now distinguishes "API succeeded with no grade" (ungraded — AI is fine) from "API call failed" (unknown state — leave the form blank with a warning instead of inventing data). Logs also dump what the metadata fetch actually returned so the matching can be diagnosed when grades don't come through

features: Schoology is now the source of truth for grade, completion date, AND feedback. Posting a grade encodes the date as a `[date: MM/DD/YYYY]` prefix on the comment so it round-trips through Schoology (the API has no native completion-date field). Re-download or open a previously-posted submission and all three fields restore from Schoology

Posting a grade now also writes the feedback to the Schoology submission comment thread — the same place Schoology UI puts teacher comments. Previously the feedback only went to the gradebook entry's comment field, which made it look invisible from the submission view. Feedback is now in both places, so it's visible wherever you look in Schoology and recoverable from either source on read
bugs: Feedback box no longer shows the student's submission text mixed with the comment thread when there's no other feedback source — the form now extracts only the teacher's messages from the thread and ignores the student's own lines

Schoology grade now actually populates the grade dropdown and points box on a graded submission — previously the form only checked for letter grades, but we send numeric points to Schoology when posting (so a graded sub came back with posted_grade="10" or "8.5", which didn't match anything in the letter dropdown). The form now splits posted_grade into a derived letter (A/B/C/D/F based on percentage) for the dropdown and the numeric value for the points box, mirroring what was originally posted
Excused/Missing exceptions from Schoology now restore as Ex/Mi in the grade dropdown

Feedback box now also falls through to the Schoology submission comment thread — most teachers leave feedback in the comment thread on the submission, not in the separate gradebook comment field, so the form was showing blank feedback for graded subs even when Schoology had it. Priority order: final feedback (user edited) → gradebook comment → submission thread → AI feedback

features: Re-download now also re-fetches the grade and teacher comment from Schoology, plus the submission comment thread — so you don't have to wait for the next full sync to see what's currently in Schoology

Re-download decides what to do based on graded state: ungraded submissions get queued for AI pre-grading on the fresh file (as before); already-graded submissions just have the Schoology grade and comment restored, with no AI run. To force a fresh AI grade on an already-graded sub, click Re-grade after the download finishes

bugs: Opening a graded submission no longer pops up "This submission already has a grade. Re-grade?" — the auto-Analyze hook was firing for any sub that didn't have the new posted_grade column populated yet, which meant freshly upgraded users got the prompt for every old graded sub without ever clicking Re-grade. The auto-Analyze gate now treats a sub as already-graded when any of posted_to_schoology, status='graded', final_grade, posted_grade, or ai_feedback is set. The overwrite prompt only appears when you explicitly click Re-grade

features: Grading window now pulls the existing grade and teacher comment from Schoology when you open a graded submission, instead of running AI to regenerate them. The form populates from Schoology by default; the AI only runs on demand

"Analyze" button is now "Re-grade" — makes it clear that AI grading is opt-in. Click Re-grade to overwrite the Schoology grade/comment with a fresh AI run; you'll be prompted to confirm before anything is replaced
Pre-grading queue now only auto-runs for submissions with no Schoology grade yet, or for resubmissions — already-graded work is left alone unless you explicitly Re-grade it

bugs: Fixed second auto-fill path that was repopulating the queue right after Cancel All — the Schoology badge refresh hook was calling enqueue_batch on every refresh and bypassing the pause check that v4.1.59 added to the other auto-grade path. The enqueue_batch call itself now respects the paused state, so any background path that tries to refill the queue (badge refresh, auto-heat, auto-grade) is silently ignored until the user resumes. Manual Analyze still works while paused

Cancel All in the grading queue now also pauses the queue — previously the queue would refill itself within seconds because the auto-grade refresh hook didn't know the user had explicitly stopped it. Resume by clicking the pause toggle
Opening a submission while the queue is paused no longer auto-starts AI analysis — the auto-Analyze-on-select hook and the auto-heat warm-up both honor the pause state now

Cancel All in the grading queue now actually stops the worker — previously it just emptied the queue while the worker kept grinding its in-flight submission for up to a minute, and the main window's "Pre-grading 1/119" pill stayed stuck during that time. Now the worker is interrupted immediately and the pill clears the moment the queue goes empty

Status line after a manual Analyze click no longer says "Pre-graded 0/0" when a single submission was successfully analyzed — priority items are now counted separately and the summary reports them as "analyzed N" so the message matches what actually happened

Re-download button now also kills any in-flight video conversion so a fresh-start request actually starts fresh — previously the v4.1.55 "don't restart for same video" guard would refuse to relaunch and the user couldn't force a clean conversion

Fixed video conversions never finishing because they kept getting cancelled and restarted on every grading-window refresh — multiple paths (auto-stale-cache, heat-worker completion, manual Re-download) all called _start_video_conversion which always cancelled the in-flight subprocess. Now it leaves an existing conversion for the same video alone instead of restarting it from zero each time

Fixed video transcription hanging mid-clip on multi-minute videos — the diagnostic confirmed whisper produced the first segment fine but then stalled on a later one. Switched to greedy decoding (beam_size=1), disabled context-feedback (condition_on_previous_text=False), and enabled VAD filtering, which are the standard mitigations for this faster-whisper failure mode. Also added per-10-segment progress breadcrumbs so a future hang is visible from the log
Also clears the persisted whisper_unavailable flag so the new settings actually get tried instead of being skipped over by the auto-disable from v4.1.53

Video conversion timeout shortened from 4 minutes to 90 seconds, and after the first timeout the app remembers that whisper is hanging on this machine and skips transcription on subsequent video opens — you'll get a frame-only preview in ~95 seconds instead of staring at "Converting video to PDF..." forever

Fixed video transcription hanging forever after "WhisperModel ready, transcribing" — faster-whisper spawns a multiprocessing resource_tracker daemon by re-running the bundled exe with python-style `-c <code>` arguments; the trampoline didn't recognize that pattern, the daemon fell through to the main app and got killed by the single-instance guard, and transcription waited forever on the dead helper. The trampoline now emulates Python's `-c` flag for these invocations

Moved the cv2 sys.path scrub directly into video_converter.py so it fires right before `import cv2` regardless of who imports the module — the scrub at main.py top wasn't sticking (something re-added Resources/cv2 to sys.path between startup and the heat worker), so the heat worker hit the recursion bug and only ever produced the placeholder "Video could not be previewed" PDF

Diagnostic: video subprocess trampoline now prints what it sees (sys.argv, the matched flag, module-run result) so we can pinpoint why a frozen subprocess falls through to full app startup instead of running the helper module
Hanging video conversions now time out after 4 minutes and fall back to a frame-only preview instead of leaving the viewer stuck on "Converting video to PDF..."
Subprocess stderr breadcrumbs (where it is in the conversion pipeline) are now tailed into the main log every poll cycle so a stuck conversion is diagnosable from the log rather than invisible

Page-strip thumbnails now actually clear on Re-download — the previous "clear" call was a silent no-op (PageStripWidget didn't have a public clear() method, so the AttributeError got swallowed and the old thumbnails stuck around)

features: While a video submission is converting, the grading window now shows the no-transcript preview immediately so the viewer isn't blank for the 30+ seconds whisper takes
bugs: Clicking Re-download or detecting a stale cache now clears the page-strip thumbnails too — previously the strip kept showing frames from the previous revision while the new file was downloading and converting
Re-download / stale-cache cleanup now also deletes the heat worker's .heat.pdf preview, so a stale preview from before the re-download can't slip into the viewer

Fixed cv2 import recursion on the macOS app — video conversion was silently degrading to a placeholder "Video could not be previewed" PDF (and the orientation OCR tiebreak was failing the same way) because cv2's own subdirectory was on sys.path, making cv2 re-import itself. Now scrubbed at startup and the bundled cv2 is collected cohesively

Fixed video transcription crashing the converter on Windows (0xC0000005 access violation in ctranslate2 4.7.x) — the bundled installer now ships ctranslate2 4.6.0, and if Whisper still can't load on a given machine the grading window now remembers and skips transcription instead of repeatedly crashing

features: When Ollama isn't available, the grading window now falls back to the Schoology submission date and awards full credit so the auto-header stamp can run end-to-end — you can still adjust either field before posting
Pre-grading queue pause/resume + a per-LP cutoff so you can stop heating work you don't plan to grade
First-time launch after a Schoology connect now asks which Learning Period to start pre-grading from
bugs: Fixed video submissions getting stuck on "Converting video to PDF..." forever — the conversion subprocess was deadlocking on its stderr pipe once whisper started writing progress; stderr now lands on a tempfile so the conversion actually completes
Fixed the macOS installer crashing on launch (the v4.1.43 DMG would not start) — PyInstaller now bundles the jaraco.* / pkg_resources / Pillow native libs the frozen app needs
Fixed video conversion in the bundled Mac app: subprocess invocations now properly route through main.py to the right module instead of re-launching the whole app
Fixed the macOS app crashing immediately on launch with "No module named 'jaraco'" — the bundled installer now includes the setuptools / pkg_resources dependencies PyInstaller was missing

Schoology pre-grading queue now correctly skips work you've already graded in Schoology — fixed the grade-reconciliation parser that was silently iterating an empty list, so 200+ already-graded submissions no longer get re-queued for AI grading

After the reconciler fix lands, Buddy auto-runs a one-time full sync at startup so existing posted-grade flags get refreshed; the auto-grader holds off until that completes so the queue never sees stale state

Cleaned up the "Could not parse stylesheet" Qt warnings printed at startup — several link-style buttons in Settings used a CSS property Qt doesn't accept (text-decoration), now using the proper Qt font underline / strike-out instead

features: Schoology auto-syncs the first time you connect, then runs a quiet weekly full sync in the background — the status bar shows progress while it runs, and an interrupted sync resumes where it left off the next time you open Buddy
Pre-grading queue now skips submissions that are already graded so you're not redownloading or re-extracting work you've already finished

Settings: split the old Integrations page into separate "File Imports" and "Schoology" pages in the Connections menu — each with a clearer ON/OFF pill toggle, and Schoology has a one-click link to the API page next to Test Connection
Video submissions now include automatic audio transcription under each frame in the rendered PDF — no extra setup needed, the model downloads on first use
bugs: Closing Buddy mid-Schoology-sync no longer leaks the in-flight HTTP requests — the sync is cancelled cleanly and resumes where it stopped

features: Send Debug Report now shows a live preview of the screenshot you're about to send — snip a new one with Win+Shift+S or Cmd+Shift+4 and the thumbnail updates on its own
Grading window: when a multi-attachment submission comes in with pages reversed, they're now auto-flipped and you get a one-click Undo instead of a prompt
Added a compact ⇅ Reverse button in the grading toolbar, visible whenever a submission has 2+ merged attachments
bugs: Fixed a crash on macOS when opening a video submission in the grading window ("recursion detected during loading of cv2") — if the OpenCV bundle fails to load, the app now falls back to a placeholder preview instead of crashing
Made the crash-report tracking sheet resilient to header row edits — data can no longer land in the wrong columns

features: Compress button now shows the current file size (e.g. "Compress (2.3 MB)") so you can see at a glance whether compression would help
Compress menu marks the current DPI level with a checkmark and bold text so you know which preset the PDF is already at
Family contact dialog has a new "Include curriculum titles" toggle that appends the curriculum name in parentheses after each course (e.g. "Algebra I (Pearson)")
bugs: Fixed a race between the grading heat worker and the main window that could raise sqlite3.InterfaceError and leave the matrix stuck on the previous Learning Period until the app was restarted

Fixed the importer error on empty WSLP rows
